paper_summary: An art-conservation case study on the deterioration and restoration of scagliola (imitation-marble decorative plaster) in Zafaran Palace, Cairo. Historic scagliola samples were characterised by digital microscopy, SEM-EDX and XRD, showing a calcite (CaCO3) dominated, heterogeneous material with cavities, microcracks and exfoliation. The authors propose a new loss-completion putty made of hollow glass microballoons mixed with Paraloid B-72 dissolved in toluene (20%) plus colour oxides and zinc, and judge it successful by visual comparison and SEM-EDX/XRD of the cured filler; no mechanical or physical property measurements of the microballoon composite are reported.
extraction_notes: Flagged off-topic for the syntactic-foam Process-Structure-Property dataset. The paper is a conservation-science case study of historical scagliola, not a materials study of hollow-particle composites. It does describe a microballoon-filled polymer putty (hollow glass microballoons in Paraloid B-72 / toluene at 20% concentration, with colour oxides and zinc, applied by spatula and cured >3 months, then sanded), which is technically a syntactic filler, but the paper reports no quantitative composite property whatsoever: no composite density, porosity, modulus, strength, particle volume or weight fraction, and no mechanical testing of any kind. The only numbers given are (a) supplier data for the microballoons themselves - bulk density 140-150 g/l, specific density 0.20 g/cm3, particle size 50 um with sizing up to 200 um; (b) EDX elemental weight/atomic percentages for the historic scagliola (Table 2: e.g. O 50.85, Ca 34.60, Si 4.27, C 5.05 wt%) and for the completion material (Table 4: Ca 70.55, O 16.06, C 6.00, Si 5.82, Al 1.04 wt%); and (c) qualitative SEM observations that the completed material has more compact grains and fewer cavities than the original. None of these are Process-Structure-Property records under the schema, so records is empty. The whole file (14 pages, through the reference list) was read; there are no property tables elsewhere in the paper.
